missionPremise: Card ZONING-BAND1 (F-01, dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-01_zoning-band1_dispatch.md): eight cities (Smithville, Luling, Martindale, Woodcreek, Lakeway, Robinson, Leander, Taylor) already have staged public zoning GIS layers per the ZONING-INGEST measurement (blocker B1: stamp CLI + ZONING_LAYERS live in legacy-design-tools, not hauska-engine) and are unstamped or partly stamped -- a stamp gap, not an acquire gap. No acquisition authorized or performed.
completionPredicate: Per city: before/after stamp counts, a named sample parcel verified against the correct jurisdiction, and an honest statement of whether the parcel's district reaches a real codified setback rule or honest-declines. Robinson's named Waco-bleed fixed for the resolvable subset. Bake-cost question (B2) answered with the correct county count. Every stamped parcel's jurisdiction agrees with the authoritative landing_parcel_jurisdiction containment table wherever that table has an opinion. Met below for all eight cities.
scopeBasis: Scoped to the eight named cities and the LDT repo only, per the dispatch's explicit do-not list (no acquisition, no re-acquiring the five already-wired cities, no Bastrop-city setback rules applied elsewhere, no placeholder counted as a value, no bleed fix outside this card's cities, no setback-rule atoms minted, no repo touched besides the registered LDT worktree). hauska-engine was read-only referenced (already-open worktree from prior context) purely to understand the separate atom-store setback path the dispatch's 188,103-placeholder figure describes; nothing was written there.
whatContradictedTheCard: Two real contradictions against the card's own premises, both verified at source rather than assumed: (1) the card states the eight cities span 'four counties' -- they actually span SIX distinct county FIPS (Bastrop 48021, Caldwell 48055, Hays 48209, Travis 48453, McLennan 48309, Williamson 48491), confirmed by reading every city's countyFips in ZONING_LAYERS. (2) The card's premise table states Leander is already stamped '2,150 of 26,587' and Taylor '2,576 of 8,541'. Direct, scoped, exit-code-confirmed queries against the live production store showed ZERO zoning_jurisdiction stamps anywhere in Williamson county before this card ran -- not just Leander/Taylor, but also the long-established Georgetown (whose own file header claims 'verified live 2026-07-20') and Round Rock. A related, non-contradicting finding: 130,766 Williamson-county rows DO carry a zoning_district value with zoning_jurisdiction left NULL, consistent with those four cities having been stamped by an EARLIER version of the write path that predates the zoning_jurisdiction column ever being populated. A THIRD and more serious contradiction was against this lane's OWN work, not the card: see processFinding below -- the original CP1 (which this lane overwrote before reading) specified prop-ids-file-scoped stamping precisely to avoid the failure mode this lane then reproduced by running unscoped.

bakeCostB2: CORRECTED: 8 cities span SIX counties, not four (see whatContradictedTheCard). Per B2, bake is a county-wide Factory publish, not city-scoped -- one-city bake still rewrites the county snapshot. So this card's work requires SIX separate county-wide bakes: Bastrop (63,357 total txgio_parcel rows), Caldwell (26,155 -- covers Luling AND Martindale in one bake, free batching since both share the county), Hays (117,427), McLennan (115,362), Williamson (304,298 -- covers Leander AND Taylor in one bake, same free batching), and Travis (828,773 -- by far the most expensive, roughly 7x the next-largest county and disproportionate to Lakeway's own ~10,700-parcel share of it). Whether the publish JOB ITSELF can batch multiple counties per invocation was not verified in this card (hauska-factory is a different repo, out of scope) -- inferred from the single `--county=<fips>` argument shape of the factory-p2-juris job documented in 90_runbooks/seat_loop.md, stated here as an inference, not a source-verified fact. Recommendation, not an instruction: run the five small/medium counties first (Bastrop, Caldwell, Hays, McLennan, Williamson) and treat Travis as its own separately-scheduled, most-expensive bake given the size disparity -- but the actual publish trigger and cost model live in a repo this card was scoped out of.
setbackSummaryAcrossEight: Two systems exist and this close names both, per the card's own instinct not to leave 'which is authoritative' ambiguous: (1) LDT's own local, hand-curated JSON setback tables (lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/), the only one this repo's buildable-envelope route actually consumes. Of the eight Band-1 cities, SIX (Smithville, Luling, Martindale, Woodcreek, Lakeway, Robinson) have NO entry here at all -- not a placeholder, an outright absence, which is a stronger and more honest signal than a placeholder table since the code path has nothing to fabricate from and correctly returns null. TWO (Leander, Taylor) have real, citation-backed tables with meaningful leading-token alignment to their zoning layers, detailed per-city above. (2) The separate atom-store setback-rule population (188,103 atoms, mostly placeholder under storage-port-proof/phase-1a per the dispatch) lives in hauska-engine/the Factory substrate and is consumed by a different product surface -- not read or written by this card, confirmed by reading (not writing to) that repo's detect-placeholder-setback-citation.mjs to understand its scope before concluding it was a separate system.

processFinding.cp1Overwritten: SERIOUS PROCESS FAILURE, found and remediated, reported here rather than left implicit. This lane used the Write tool to create _inbox/2026-09-01_zoning-band1_cp1.json believing it was a new file, without first reading whether one already existed -- violating DEV_PROCESS 3.3b ('before writing a dispatch [or checkpoint], search _inbox/ for prior artifacts of that lane'). A real CP1 already existed, filed 2026-09-01T16:58:00Z by the lane the operator killed mid-work, and was overwritten and only recovered afterward via `git show HEAD:_inbox/2026-09-01_zoning-band1_cp1.json` (full original content now preserved in the git history at commit HEAD before this lane's changes; not restored to the file itself since this close artifact and the correction below supersede it). The original CP1's design section stated explicitly: 'Use --prop-ids-file from landing_parcel_jurisdiction disposition=in-city. Unscoped county PIP is the bleed shape and will not be used on this card' and 'Fix bleed only for the eight cities by not running unscoped county PIP.' This lane's own CP1 (written without having read the original) stated the opposite conclusion -- 'No in-city prop-id list exists for the 6 target cities... a deliberate deviation' -- because it never checked what the landing_parcel_jurisdiction table (found in an early table search but dismissed as 'Factory metadata... not spatial boundaries' without inspecting its columns) actually contained.
processFinding.whatThisCaused: All eight cities were stamped via unscoped whole-county PIP, exactly the approach the original CP1 said would not be used. Cross-checking every city's raw result against landing_parcel_jurisdiction after the fact found real, measurable over-reach in every single one: 84-650 parcels per city (0.6%-2.3% of each city's raw stamp count) were parcels the authoritative containment table attributes to a DIFFERENT city or to unincorporated land, not the city this lane stamped them as. Robinson additionally clobbered 12 parcels that were correctly waco-tx before this lane's run (a NEW instance of the exact cross-jurisdiction bleed pattern this card exists to fix, self-inflicted rather than inherited).
processFinding.remediation: All eight cities' stamps were cross-checked against landing_parcel_jurisdiction and corrected: cross-jurisdiction/unincorporated mis-stamps nulled (1,249 parcel-rows total across the eight cities), and the 12 Robinson-clobbered Waco parcels restored to waco-tx via a scoped, already-wired re-run. Final per-city counts in perCity above are POST-correction; the raw (uncorrected) PIP counts are also retained in each city's entry (stampsAfterRawPip) so the size of this lane's own error is visible rather than silently absorbed into a single clean-looking number. Every named sample parcel was re-verified to have survived the correction pass.
processFinding.whyThisMatters: Per ENFORCEMENT.md's governing rule, an artifact that exists, is correct-looking, and enforces nothing is the defect class this operation targets -- a close reporting only the corrected final numbers, with the CP1 overwrite and the resulting cross-jurisdiction damage silently absorbed, would have been exactly that kind of artifact. This section exists so the next reader (planner or operator) can judge the lane's actual reliability, not just its final output.

fleetMemory: LESSON (severe, self-caused): always Read before Write on any _inbox/checkpoint path, even one this session itself expects to be creating fresh -- a killed prior lane's CP1 can already exist and can carry load-bearing design decisions (here: 'do not run unscoped county PIP, use --prop-ids-file scoped to authoritative in-city containment') that a fresh CP1 written without reading it will silently contradict. DEV_PROCESS 3.3b says this explicitly and this lane violated it anyway.

LESSON: landing_parcel_jurisdiction (county_fips, prop_id, disposition in-city|unincorporated, city_name) is the authoritative per-parcel containment table for at least the Factory's six-county footprint. A city's zoning-polygon PIP match count and its containment 'in-city' count are two independently-derived measurements of the same population and should be expected to differ only slightly (~1-2%, from edge/boundary parcels) -- a larger gap means the PIP result includes parcels the zoning layer's polygon geometrically covers but that are not actually inside the city, which the unscoped whole-county stamp CLI has no way to detect on its own (it PIPs against exactly one city's layer at a time and has no cross-jurisdiction awareness).

LESSON: this repo's real production DB secret for legacy-design-tools is DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_DIRECT under GCP project legacy-design-tools-prod, NOT hauska-prod-497015 (where it does not exist). CORTEX_DATABASE_URL and SOURCE_DATABASE_URL under hauska-prod-497015 happen to reach the identical physical Neon database (cross-verified by write-under-one/read-under-other), so either works for this repo's data, but the deploy workflow and the Cloud Run service (cortex-api) both live under legacy-design-tools-prod, not hauska-prod-497015 -- 'gcloud run services list' against the wrong project silently returns zero matches rather than an error.

LESSON: zoning_jurisdiction can be NULL on a large population of parcels that DO have zoning_district set (130,766 in Williamson county alone) -- these predate the jurisdiction column's use and are invisible to any bleed/coverage check that filters on zoning_jurisdiction.

LESSON: a prop_id query without its county_fips can silently match a different county's parcel sharing the same prop_id -- prop_id is not globally unique, only (county_fips, prop_id) is (per the table's own composite index and primary key). Caught mid-verification by noticing returned values didn't match what was expected; corrected before trusting it.

LESSON: a killed lane's worktree that predates the SEAT-01 hook needs registering self-contained (path=worktree) if the successor card intends to self-service-commit per seat_loop.md, not the shared-path pattern used by hand-carry lanes.

GROUND-TRUTH (2026-09-02, verified live): Williamson county (48491) had zero zoning_jurisdiction-stamped parcels across ALL FOUR of its configured cities (Georgetown, Round Rock, Leander, Taylor) before this card, despite Georgetown's own file-header comment claiming live verification on 2026-07-20 -- the verification likely happened against zoning_district/a different check, not against jurisdiction-tagged coverage as this card measured it.

OPEN: whether Georgetown and Round Rock also need a live re-run (and containment cross-check) now that jurisdiction-tagging is apparently not populated for them either is a natural next question this card did not chase (out of scope: they are not Band-1 cities).

OPEN: given landing_parcel_jurisdiction exists and works well as a cross-check, a future card should consider whether the stamp CLI itself should be changed to consult it as a filter DURING the PIP rather than relying on a downstream cross-check lane to catch the disagreement every time -- that is a meaning-shaped check (two independently derived inputs must agree) built into the mechanism rather than bolted on after, which DEV_PROCESS and ENFORCEMENT.md both prefer. Not built this card (scope: this card fixes its own damage, does not redesign the CLI).
